hints: Notice the key condition is hot aqueous sodium hydroxide, so think about which disproportionation reaction of chlorine this gives.

Recall the balanced equation for hot NaOH is $3\text{Cl}_2 + 6\text{NaOH} \rightarrow 5\text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$, so find the mole ratio of $\text{Cl}_2$ to $\text{NaClO}_3$.
Convert your moles of $\text{NaClO}_3$ to mass using $m = n \times M_r$ with $M_r$ of $\text{NaClO}_3$ about 106.5.
walkthrough:
**Spot the hot NaOH reaction**

Chlorine disproportionates differently in cold and hot alkali. With hot concentrated NaOH, chlorate(V) is formed.

$$3\text{Cl}_2 + 6\text{NaOH} \rightarrow 5\text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Use the 3 to 1 mole ratio**

From the equation, 3 mol of $\text{Cl}_2$ make only 1 mol of $\text{NaClO}_3$. So divide your chlorine moles by 3.

$$n(\text{NaClO}_3) = \frac{0.600}{3} = 0.200 \text{ mol}$$

**Convert moles to mass**

Now calculate $M_r$ of $\text{NaClO}_3$ and multiply by moles. This gives the final mass.

$$M_r = 23.0 + 35.5 + (3 \times 16.0) = 106.5$$
$$m = 0.200 \times 106.5 = 21.3 \text{ g}$$

options.A: Correct. 0.600 mol Cl2 gives 0.200 mol NaClO3 by the 3:1 ratio, and 0.200 x 106.5 = 21.3 g.
options.B: False. This is the mass of NaClO from the cold NaOH reaction. Cold conditions give $\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$, so 0.600 mol gives 0.600 x 74.5 = 44.7 g. The question states hot, so chlorate, $\text{NaClO}_3$, forms instead.
options.C: False. This assumes a 1:1 ratio of $\text{Cl}_2$ to $\text{NaClO}_3$ (0.600 x 106.5 = 63.9 g). It forgets the balanced equation needs 3 mol of $\text{Cl}_2$ for every 1 mol of chlorate.
options.D: False. This is roughly double the 1:1 answer, from assuming 1 mol of $\text{Cl}_2$ makes 2 mol of $\text{NaClO}_3$ (1.20 x 106.5 = 127.8 g). The correct ratio is 3 mol $\text{Cl}_2$ to 1 mol $\text{NaClO}_3$.
